description_ru: Анна и Бен спорят, куда поехать летом, и находят компромисс между горами и городом.
text:
Anna: Okay, we've been talking about this for two weeks, and we still haven't booked anything. Where should we go this summer?
Ben: I've told you many times, I want to go to the mountains. Imagine fresh air, quiet villages, and long walks every day. If we went to Austria, we could even stay in a cabin by a lake.
Anna: A cabin by a lake sounds lovely for about two days. Then I would be bored. I want a city with museums, restaurants and street musicians. What about Lisbon?
Ben: Lisbon is beautiful, but it will be crowded and hot in July. Last time we visited a big city in summer, you complained about the heat for a week.
Anna: That's not true! I complained for three days. And you spent the whole trip looking for a bench in the shade.
Ben: Fair enough. Let's make a list, then. What do we both want from the holiday?
Anna: I want good food, some culture and a bit of adventure. And I don't want to spend the whole time in a car.
Ben: I want to relax, to see some nature, and to avoid crowds. And to be honest, I would like to spend less money than last year. We went over the budget by almost four hundred euros.
Anna: Because you bought that ridiculous hat in Florence.
Ben: It was a very good hat. Anyway, what if we found a place that combines both? A small city near the mountains, perhaps?
Anna: Hmm. Like Innsbruck? It has an old town, great cafés, and the mountains are right behind it. We could take a cable car in the morning and have dinner in the city in the evening.
Ben: That's a clever idea. I've heard that you can hike to a little restaurant on top of a hill, and the view is supposed to be incredible.
Anna: Then we could do both. But how would we get there? Flights are expensive in summer, and I don't want to drive for ten hours.
Ben: We could take the train. I've read that the night train from Berlin has sleeping cabins. It takes longer, but we would save the cost of a hotel for one night.
Anna: I like that. Sleeping on a train is romantic, as long as nobody snores. My cousin travelled that way last year, and he said that the man in the next cabin sounded like a tractor.
Ben: If that happens, we'll buy earplugs. Now, what about accommodation? Hotels in the centre will be pricey.
Anna: We could look for a small guesthouse a little further out. Some of them include breakfast, and the owners often give you good tips about local places.
Ben: Good point. I've stayed in a guesthouse in Slovenia once, and the owner took us to a hidden waterfall that wasn't in any guidebook.
Anna: See, that's the kind of adventure I mean. Okay, let me check the dates. I can take the holiday from the fifth to the nineteenth of July. Is that possible for you?
Ben: I haven't asked my boss yet, but I don't think it will be a problem. If I tell her this week, she will probably agree. Everyone wants August off, so July is easier.
Anna: Perfect. How long should we stay in each place? I'd say four days in the city and five in the mountains.
Ben: I'd prefer the opposite, but let's compromise. Five days in the mountains, four in the city, and three days travelling.
Anna: That adds up to twelve. We have fourteen. What shall we do with the other two days?
Ben: We could add a stop in Munich on the way back. I've always wanted to see the big beer gardens.
Anna: Of course you have. Fine, but only if we also visit the art museum. There's a famous collection of modern paintings there.
Ben: Deal. And if the weather is bad in the mountains, we'll spend a day in the museums in Innsbruck instead.
Ben: One more thing. Should we rent bikes in the city? I've heard that Innsbruck has special paths along the river.
Anna: Good idea, as long as the bikes have gears. I've never liked pushing a bike uphill.
Anna: Wonderful. So, let's decide who does what. I'll look at trains and tickets, and you can search for guesthouses.
Ben: Agreed. But we'll have to be quick. If we wait another week, the prices will probably go up.
Anna: Then let's do it tonight. I'll open the laptop and you'll make the tea.
Ben: I knew it. You always give me the easy job.
Anna: That's because you make terrible travel plans but excellent tea.
Ben: I'll accept that compliment. Shall we say dinner first, and bookings afterwards?
Anna: Yes. And I'm paying for the dinner, since you won the argument about the mountains.
Ben: Did I win? I thought we both won.
Anna: That's the right answer. Come on, let's go.

questions.question: Where does Ben want to go at first?
questions.answer: He wants to go to the mountains, for example Austria.

questions.question: Why does Anna not want only the mountains?
questions.answer: She would be bored and wants museums, restaurants and music.

questions.question: How do they decide to travel?
questions.answer: They plan to take the night train.

questions.question: Who does which task at the end?
questions.answer: Anna looks at trains and Ben searches for guesthouses.
